text:
Sean Couturier has one goal in 27 games, and it isn't for lack of looks. He has 4.18 expected goals, our measure of chance quality, so he is about three goals short of what those chances usually produce, and he is shooting 3%. Our numbers flag him as due. In his last ten games he has no goals and four assists while playing about 15 minutes a night, with 0.89 expected goals in one loss to Edmonton alone.

At 33, Couturier is a checking center now more than a scorer, and that part of his game still shows. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.17 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, 96th percentile among forwards, the same strength that won him the 2019-20 Selke. This season the Flyers have had 44.9% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, slightly better than without him. Our numbers project 32 points, with 10 goals in the middle of his range. Shooting percentage is the noisiest number in the sport; the chances are the part to trust.
headline: Couturier keeps getting chances and getting nothing
